title: Text encoders: CLIP, T5 and LLM encoders

questions.q: In ComfyUI's code, what can token 3 see in CLIP?
options: Tokens 0 to 3: the mask is causal
questions.answer: Tokens 0 to 3: the mask is causal
questions.why: clip_model.py adds triu of a large negative number to the scores.

questions.q: What does a diffusion model usually get from a text encoder?
options: A row for every token, and sometimes a pooled vector too
questions.answer: A row for every token, and sometimes a pooled vector too
questions.why: SD 1.5 gets [1, 77, 768]. The pooled vector is separate, on families that use it.

questions.q: Your SD 1.5 prompt has 76 tokens. What tensor does it make?
questions.why: 75 fit one chunk, so the 76th starts a second, joined along tokens.

questions.q: Why is the width 7680 on Klein 4B?
options: It pads to the latent size
Three of Qwen3's hidden layers are placed side by side, each 2560 wide
questions.answer: Three of Qwen3's hidden layers are placed side by side, each 2560 wide

questions.q: Where does CLIP's pooled vector come from?
options: The row at the end token
questions.answer: The row at the end token
questions.why: clip_model.py indexes by where eos_token_id first appears, or by num_tokens.

questions.q: Which of these has no 77-token chunking?
questions.why: T5 uses a huge max_length and a minimum, so it's one sequence.
